From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Positions and Disclosure Letter

**Scope and caveats:** This review is based on the Seller's update summary and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). I have not seen the full SPA clauses, the underlying data room documents (DD-002 to DD-012), or the draft funds flow. Statutory points (Privacy Act, NSW payroll tax, limitation periods) should be confirmed by NSW counsel before we rely on them.

## Overall assessment

The package moves most of the known risk onto the Buyer. The Seller has disclosed the problems in the data room but is pairing that disclosure with clauses that stop the Buyer recovering for them. The main mechanism is a combination of general disclosure of the whole data room, a buyer-knowledge bar (cl 8.3), and a general cap and time limit applied to everything. Several known issues are unresolved at the date of the letter, and the Seller is treating them as post-Completion problems.

## Key departures from the Buyer's interests

### 1. Disclosure architecture (Disclosure Letter cl 1.1, 1.2; Schedule 7; cl 8.3)
- **Problem:** Disclosing "every fact... contained or referred to" in the entire data room, plus public registers, would disclose almost any breach. Combined with cl 8.3, the Buyer would be barred from claiming for anything in the data room, which is nearly all of the diligence record.
- **Pushback:** Delete general disclosure of the data room and public registers. Disclosure should be specific, fairly disclosed against a specific warranty, and not a general reference to documents. Delete cl 8.3 entirely. If the Seller insists on a knowledge concept, limit it to actual knowledge of named deal-team members, not "advisers" or "discoverable" matters, and state expressly that it does not apply to specific indemnities or the fundamental warranties.

### 2. Caps and thresholds (cl 12.1, 12.2)
- **General cap:** 20% (AUD 4.8m) is high for a general warranty cap. Expect the Seller to resist moving this, but the Buyer should open lower, in line with market norms for this deal size, and not accept 20% as a baseline. Fundamental warranties should be capped at the full purchase price.
- **De minimis (AUD 25k) and basket (AUD 250k, deductible structure):** A deductible basket of AUD 250k means the Buyer absorbs the first AUD 250k of any warranty losses. Several known issues (bonuses at AUD 420k, Ironquay AUD 180k, supplier renewals AUD 330k) would each be partly or wholly absorbed by the basket if they were treated as warranty claims. Pushback: move to a tipping basket (once exceeded, full recovery), reduce the basket, and exclude known or specifically identified matters from both the de minimis and the basket.

### 3. Time limits (cl 12.3, 13)
- **18 months** for general warranties is short, particularly for tax and IP matters where issues often surface after a full audit cycle. Pushback: at least 24 months for general warranties, with tax warranties and tax indemnity running to 60 days after the relevant ATO amendment period expires.
- **"Any limitation applies to all Claims":** Reject. Time limits must not apply to fundamental warranties, tax, or specific indemnities, which should run for the statutory period or longer.

### 4. Fundamental and title warranties
- The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the general cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity." This is a material concession. Title to 100% of the shares is the core asset of the deal.
- **Pushback:** Title, capacity, and authority should sit outside all general caps and time limits, with liability capped at the full purchase price. Consider a 6-year period, which aligns with the NSW contractual limitation period under the Limitation Act 1969 (NSW); confirm with counsel.

### 5. Exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)
- These apply to "all Claims of any nature," which would include fraud. Pushback: carve out fraud (including fraud by the Seller's officers and advisers) and wilful misconduct from the limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions. Specific indemnities should also sit outside the exclusive remedy.

### 6. Known issues not adequately addressed

**a) Bluefen change-control consent (cl 3, 6.3; DD-002; Disclosure cl 2)**
- Bluefen represents roughly 30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m). The Seller has not produced the final written consent or evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- The Seller's proposal is "reasonable endeavours" and treating consent as satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent." That is a weaker standard than a true condition precedent, and it does not require the conditions to be satisfied.
- **Pushback:** Make a final written Bluefen consent, with evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied (or waived in writing by the Buyer), a condition precedent. Include a termination right if not delivered by a long-stop date. Consider a price adjustment or escrow if consent is granted subject to conditions with cost.

**b) Riverlark facility (cl 2, 7; DD-003; Disclosure cl 3)**
- Roughly AUD 3.2m outstanding, with no discharge of security yet. The Seller proposes that the release be provided "following Completion."
- On a debt-free/cash-free basis, this debt must be repaid from the price at Completion, not left in the Company after it. Post-Completion releases leave the Buyer exposed to the lender's security and a potential enforcement or default position.
- **Pushback:** Require a payoff letter and executed discharge of all security (including PPSR registrations) delivered at Completion, with the payoff amount deducted from the price. Confirm the funds flow reflects this.

**c) Employee bonuses (DD-005; Disclosure cl 5; funds flow)**
- AUD 420,000 in conditional Completion bonuses are not in the draft funds flow. The disclosure is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- These are debt-like items under a cash-free/debt-free price. The Seller's position that they are "a matter for the Seller" does not work if the Company will pay them after Completion.
- **Pushback:** Treat the bonuses and all associated employer costs (payroll tax, super, on-costs) as debt or a price deduction in the completion accounts, or have the Seller fund them. Verify NSW payroll tax exposure with the tax team; it should not be assumed to be nil. Require a full schedule of change-of-control, retention and bonus arrangements as a warranty.

**d) Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DD-004, DD-010; Disclosure cl 4)**
- Under DD-004 cl 7.3, SOW3 Project Materials do not transfer until every SOW3 fee is paid. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 as open, with no receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment on file.
- The Seller's indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and called "adequate." It does not address IP ownership or title to the materials, and the Company may not own the code it relies on.
- **Pushback:** (i) Seller to pay the AUD 180,000 (or confirm the true amount) before Completion, with evidence; (ii) obtain a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay as a condition precedent; (iii) specific indemnity for any third-party IP claim relating to SOW3 and related work, outside the cap and time limits; (iv) IP ownership warranty specifically covering the SOW3 materials.

**e) Export / privacy incident (cl 4.6, Schedule 6; DD-006; Disclosure cl 6)**
- Possible unauthorised disclosure of ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps), sent to an unintended external address. The Seller calls this "preliminary" and "not expected to be material," but the investigation is incomplete: it is not known whether anyone accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required.
- Under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), an eligible data breach may trigger a notification obligation to the OAIC and affected individuals. Regulatory, notification and remediation costs, and any claims by individuals, could fall on the Company after Completion.
- **Pushback:** (i) Seller to commission an independent forensic review before signing or as a condition precedent, with findings provided to the Buyer; (ii) specific indemnity for all losses arising from the incident (regulatory costs, notification, remediation, claims), outside the basket, cap, and time limits; (iii) warranty that no notifiable data breach has occurred, disclosed specifically; (iv) escrow or retention sized to the exposure once quantified.

**f) Office lease (cl 7; DD-007; Disclosure cl 7)**
- A notification obligation exists, but the Seller has not confirmed whether landlord consent to the share sale is required.
- **Pushback:** Seller to confirm in writing; if consent is required, it becomes a condition precedent. Obtain a landlord comfort letter.

**g) Mossvale assignment restriction (DD-009; Disclosure cl 9)**
- The Seller says the restriction is on assignment and does not state that consent is required merely because shares are sold. Our reading should be confirmed against the actual clause, since a change-of-control trigger may exist elsewhere in the document.
- **Pushback:** Specific warranty that no consent is required for the share sale under the Mossvale agreement, or obtain consent as a CP.

**h) Supplier renewals (DD-008, DD-011; Disclosure cl 8)**
- Three related renewals totalling AUD 330,000 are described as ordinary course. The disclosure does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, or accrued.
- **Pushback:** Require the Seller to classify each renewal, confirm whether any commitment extends beyond Completion, and address any non-ordinary-course element through the price or working capital mechanism. Treat splitting of related renewals with caution: the Seller has read them "together for timing/scope," which suggests they may be one commitment.

**i) Title to shares (DD-012; Disclosure cl 10)**
- The Seller relies on the share register showing Harbourglass as holder of 100%. The register is evidence, not verification.
- **Pushback:** Buyer to complete independent checks: ASIC company search, inspection of original share certificates and the register, PPSR search for encumbrances over the shares, and confirmation of no pre-emptive or option rights. Seller warranty of full legal and beneficial ownership, free of encumbrances, outside general limits.

**j) Tax and IP warranties (Seller summary)**
- The Seller treats tax and IP as "settled under the general regime." They are not settled. Both should be subject to specific indemnities and extended time limits, as noted above.

## Recommendations (summary)

**Priority 1: Must resolve before signing or as conditions precedent**
1. Delete general data-room and public-register disclosure and cl 8.3 buyer-knowledge bar.
2. Bluefen final written consent and satisfaction of cl 11.3 conditions as a CP, with termination right.
3. Riverlark payoff letter and security discharge at Completion, deducted from price.
4. Confirmatory Ironquay assignment and payment of the AUD 180k (or verified amount) as a CP.
5. Independent forensic review of the DD-006 incident.
6. Treatment of AUD 420k bonuses and employer costs as debt-like items in the price.

**Priority 2: Specific indemnities (outside cap, basket and time limits)**
7. Ironquay IP and SOW3 materials.
8. Privacy/export incident.
9. Pre-Completion tax liabilities and payroll tax on bonuses.
10. Any lease or Mossvale consent issues that prove to require consent.

**Priority 3: Structural protections**
11. Title, capacity and authority: outside all caps and time limits, capped at full price.
12. Fraud carve-out from all limitation, exclusive remedy and non-reliance clauses.
13. General cap: open lower than 20%; fundamental cap at full price.
14. Basket: convert to tipping basket and reduce; exclude specifically disclosed matters from de minimis and basket.
15. Time limits: extend general warranties to at least 24 months; tax to the ATO amendment period plus buffer; reject "all Claims subject to all limitations."
16. Escrow or retention, sized once the privacy and Bluefen exposures are quantified.

**Priority 4: Verification**
17. Complete independent title checks (ASIC, PPSR, share certificates).
18. Confirm supplier renewal classification and any lease/Mossvale consent triggers against the source documents.
19. NSW counsel to confirm statutory points (Privacy Act notification, payroll tax, Limitation Act periods, duty) before finalising the mark-up.

**Negotiating note:** The Seller's package is framed as "fair and balanced," but it leaves the Buyer with most of the known downside. Expect the Seller to argue that known issues should be priced rather than indemnified. The Buyer's response should be that the known issues are either priced (bonuses, Ironquay fees, Riverlark debt, supplier renewals, where quantified) or indemnified (unquantified exposures: privacy, Bluefen consent conditions, IP ownership, tax), and not left to the warranty regime, which the buyer-knowledge bar would defeat.
